China noun

Renaissance

M-O s.v. China (Wolff, 1726)

Sinae, Sinārum m.

noun, first declension

A country takes a preposition: in Sinās, in Sinīs, ex Sinīs. Properly the people, the Chinese, used as the name of the land: Sinārum imperātōrēs (Wolff, in M-O). Modern Latin often writes a long ī; we leave it unmarked, having found no quantity in our sources.

Other words

    declension · modern · Traupman 122; M-O s.v. Chinese (Egger)

  • Sēres, Sērum m. — the Chinese, as the Romans knew them, the silk people

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Verg. G. 2.121 (Lewis & Short); Hor. C. 3.29.27 (Lewis & Short)

  • Sinicus, Sinica, Sinicum — Chinese

    declension · also used · Renaissance · M-O s.v. Chinese (Wolff, 1726)
